summary.intent: Address four open review findings (two Medium, two Low) on PR #43, all in parse.rs, by dispatching an agent to fix them on the PR branch.
summary.outcome: The assistant read the findings, launched an agent to fix them (delete the bracket scan, add a note for the debug_assertions use, add a distinct 'too large' reason), and summarized the plan. The fixes were not yet reported as completed in this transcript.

repo: PR #42's depth-scanner tests will conflict once #43 lands because the function they test is being deleted; merge #43 first, then update #42 to drop those tests.
Entire is used to track review findings; resolved findings get a note each, and trails (e.g. 184, 200) track sweep work.
The 'heuristics stated as facts' pattern was flagged by a sweep and counts toward trail 184's remaining work.
Previous worst-case hostile input cost was 424 MiB and 0.08 s; the agent's acceptance threshold is about 1 GiB or 2 s.

code.finding: Medium: a backslash-CRLF string continuation ends the string early in the bracket scan, so a valid file with 257 '(' inside it is falsely rejected.
Medium: after postfix '++', a division is mistaken for a regex, so a valid function with 256 lines of 'count++ / total' is falsely rejected. No scan can decide regex versus division.
Low: cfg!(debug_assertions) is used to mean 'unoptimized'; needs a note next to the constant and in the decision log.
Low: a file over about 254 KiB is degraded the same as a parse error with no named reason; should get a distinct 'too large' reason in the core result.

workflow: Prefer deleting a heuristic scan that is redundant with an existing guarantee (the per-byte stack proof bounds recursion) rather than patching each blind spot.
Have the agent measure hostile-case cost before committing to the deletion, with stop-and-report thresholds.
Push fixes to the PR branch as a fast-forward and rewrite the PR description to match.
Multiple agents can run in parallel (here the #43 fix and the copy-drift PR for trail 200).

friction: The assistant ran two Bash commands to show the findings (a second with an explicit trail selector), suggesting the first did not show the full text as wanted.
open_items: After #43 merges, update #42 to drop the depth-scanner tests whose mutation no longer exists.
If the post-deletion worst case exceeds about 1 GiB or 2 s, the agent will stop and report rather than proceed.
Trail 184 still has remaining work on 'heuristics stated as facts'.
The copy-drift PR (trail 200) is being handled by a separate running agent.
